text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government is incapable of dealing with a crime wave which began after the last general elections, a commentary said.
- A 67-year-old woman died in crossfire and 10 people were wounded in a gunfight between rival gangs in the Albanian port city of Durres on Thursday.
- Zef Brozi, the former supreme court chairman, denies he had asked for opposition leader Fatos Nano's imprisonment. He accuses President Sali Berisha of putting his rival in prison.
- Nine parliamentarians of the opposition Socialists and two of the ethnic Greek Human Rights Party have still not taken up their seats in the parliament.
- No Socialist Party fraction was planning to create a new party, Ilir Meta, one of its leaders said in a news conference.
- Following the last Pristina-Belgrade agreement on education, Yugoslav charge d'affaires in Tirana Stanimir Vukicevic said better relations were expected between the two countries.
- The United States is concerned about Albania's democratic development after the May 26 elections, criticised for alleged irregularities.
- Former senior communist officials, sentenced to jail for crimes against humanity, will appeal to the European court in Strasbourg, one of their lawyers said.

- The Albanian parliament passed a law which would allow the armed forces to send a unit of 50 troops to serve in peacekeeping missions in Zadar, Croatia, alongside German troops in the NATO-led peace implementation force for Bosnia.
- The Canadian company Nebex is looking for gold in northern Albania.
- Parliament ratified a memorandum signed in May 8, 1992 between Albania and Britain on the return of 1,574 kg of gold stolen by the Nazis in World War Two.
- Finance minister Ridvan Bode has sacked 27 employees in a reshuffle of his staff.
